_README: Pronunciation reference sheet for ad narration (Kokoro af_heart).
Kokoro's grapheme-to-phoneme pass mangles federal jargon it has never
seen. Each rule respells a term PHONETICALLY for the synthesizer only —
on-screen text and captions are untouched, so they still show the real
spelling. Patterns are case-insensitive regex, applied in order, so a
plural rule MUST come before its singular or the singular eats the stem.
Provenance: seeded from the curated list in the main app's
video/narrate.py, which was validated by ear across the instructional
video catalogue. Vendored rather than imported — the import was a path
to a sibling checkout that does not exist on a CI runner, so it silently
did nothing there and every ad the pipeline rendered went out with no
Adding a term: run scripts/check_pronunciation.py to see the phonemes
before and after. Do not guess a respelling — check it.
_READS_CORRECTLY_NOTE: Tokens that need no rule because Kokoro already says them right.
Every one was checked against its phonemes via
scripts/check_pronunciation.py — this is not a wishlist, and an
entry added without checking defeats the coverage gate.
It is production data, not a test fixture: narration.build()
consults it to decide whether a Claude-drafted script is sayable
before that script is ever synthesized.
